:J U D G M E N T:
This is a claim petition U/Sec.166 of MV Act claiming compensation of Rs.18,00,000/- with interest for the injuries suffered by the petitioner in the Motor Vehicle Accident occurred on 22.08.2021.
2.

The averments of the petition in brief is as follows:
On 22.08.2021 at about 11.45 a.m., when the petitioner was riding the TVS XL bearing Reg.No.KA-41-E-9463 slowly by observing all the traffic rules near Mekhri Circle, Ramanamaharshi road, Bangalore, at that time all of a sudden the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-04-MW-9940 was driven by its driver with high speed in a rash or negligent manner and dashed against the above said TVS XL from behind.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately,
the petitioner was shifted to Columbia Asia Hospital, Bangalore, after first aid he was shifted to St. Theresa's Hospital, Bangalore, wherein he was treated as an inpatient.
The petitioner has spent Rs.3,50,000/- towards medical and nourishment expenses.
He has to undergone future treatment and has to incur future medical expenses.
Further, the petitioner has suffered permanent disability, he is unable to lead normal life prior to the accident and suffered loss of income.
Further, the accident was occurred due to rash or negligent driving of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-04-MW-9940 by its driver.
The Sadashivanagar Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of above said Car.
Further, at the time of accident, the 1st respondent is the insurer and the 2 nd respondent is the R.C. owner of offending vehicle.
Hence, both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, this petition.

3. In response to the notice issued by the Tribunal, the 1st respondent/insurer appeared through its Raju Chapparamane vs Universal Sampo Gen Ins Co Ltd on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60763186/
2 counsel and filed written statement.

sentences.text: It is relevant to note that, during the pendency of the proceedings, petitioner impleaded ICICI Lombard Insurance Company as respondent No.3.
Accordingly 1st respondent namely Universal Sompo General Insurance Company has been deleted from the cause title.
The 2 nd respondent/R.C. owner of offending vehicle remained absent and he has been placed Ex-parte.
The 3rd respondent/insurer appeared through its counsel and filed written statement.

4. The written statement averments of the 3 rd respondent are hereunder:
This respondent has denied the issuance of insurance policy with respect to Car bearing Reg.No.KA-04-MW-9940, inter-alia contended that, if the petitioner establishes the insurance policy to the above said car, the liability to indemnification is subject to terms and conditions of the policy, provisions of M.V. Act, valid and effective driving licence possessed by the driver of the said vehicle, valid R.C. and F.C.
It is contended that, there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and Sec.158(6) of M.V. Act.
Further contended that, the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-04- MW-9940 was not at all involved in the accident and the driver of the said vehicle is no way related to the accident.
The police have filed charge sheet against the offending vehicle by colluding with the petitioner and owner of the said vehicle.
It is contended that, the driver of offending Car was not holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.

This respondent has denied the date, time, rash or negligent driving of the offending vehicle, age, occupation and income of the petitioner, injuries and disability sustained, treatment taken and amount spent by the petitioner.
Further contended that, the alleged accident was occurred due to self negligence of the petitioner and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-04-MW-9940.
With these contentions, 3rd respondent prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings, the predecessor in the office has framed the following :ISSUES:
1.

Whether Respondent No.1 proves that, Insurance policy of the vehicle was in force from 24.10.2019 to 23.10.2022 only, and therefore, it is not liable to pay compensation?
2. Whether the petitioner proves that he sustained injuries on 22.08.2021 due to rash and negligent driving of Car bearing registration No.KA-04-MW-9940 by its driver as contended in the petition?
3. Whether the petitioner proves that he is entitled for the compensation? If so, to what extent and from whom?
4. What order or award?

8. ISSUE No.1 :- Initially the petitioner made Universal Sompo General Insurance Co. Ltd., as 1 st respondent.

9. ISSUE No.2 :-
According to the petitioner, he has sustained injuries in the road accident.
The accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-MW-9940.
In order to prove this issue, the petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 by way of filing affidavit in support of his oral examination-in-chief.
Hence, this Tribunal need not to recapitulate the same once again at this juncture.
P.W.1 has relied on Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.6 and Ex.P.10.
Accordingly, Ex.P.1 is the true copy of FIR.

10. According to the respondent No.3, the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-04-MW-9940 was not at all involved in the accident and the driver of the said vehicle is no way related to the accident.

The alleged accident was occurred due to self negligence of the petitioner and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-04-MW-9940.
11.

Further, to prove the alleged negligence on the part of petitioner, the Insurance Company has cross-examined Raju Chapparamane vs Universal Sampo Gen Ins Co Ltd on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60763186/

sentences.text: Nothing has been elicited from mouth of P.W.1 to establish that the accident was took place only on the negligence of petitioner.
Likewise, the 3rd respondent neither examined the driver of offending vehicle nor ocular witnesses to the incident to establish its defence.
Hence, the 3rd respondent has failed to establish the negligence on the part of petitioner.

12. At this juncture it is worth to refer the decision reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 between Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that, "it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied".

13. Again it is worth to rely on the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka reported in ILR 2003 Karnataka page 493, between Mallamma Vs. Balaji and Others, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held at para 12 as hereunder:
" Filing of the charge sheet against the driver is also a prima-facie case to hold that,
the driver of the said lorry was responsible for the accident and burden shifts on him to prove the same".
14.
In the instant case, the petitioner has produced police documents.
As per Ex.P.2, complaint was lodged before the Sadashivanagar Traffic Police Station.
Thereafter, as per Ex.P.1, FIR was lodged against the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-04-MW-9940.

On careful perusal of Ex.P.1, Ex.P.2 and Ex.P.6, it appears to this Tribunal that, on the basis of complaint, the police have registered the case against the driver of the offending vehicle and Investigating officer has submitted Charge sheet as per Ex.P.6 after completing investigation.

A careful perusal of Ex.P.10, it clearly goes to show that,
the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

Further, on perusal of Ex.P.6 i.e.,
charge sheet
, it reveals that, the driver of offending vehicle i.e., Car bearing Reg.No.KA-04- MW-9940 has been arrayed as an accused.
The above referred decisions are aptly applicable to the case on hand.
In the instant case also, the charge sheet has been filed against the diver of offending vehicle.

15. At the cost of repetition, the contents of complaint and charge sheet clearly reveals that, when the petitioner was riding the TVS XL bearing Reg.No.KA-41-E-9463, the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-04-MW-9940 came in a rash or negligent manner with high and dashed against the above said TVS XL.
The evidence placed on record is clearly goes to show that driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-04-MW-9940 has caused the accident.
Accordingly, Issue No.2 is answered in the Affirmative.
16. ISSUE No.3:- Already this Tribunal has observed that, the accident was caused due to the rash or negligent driving of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-04-MW-9940.
It is needless to mention that,
already
this Tribunal has observed that, 3rd respondent is the insurer and the 2 nd respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

sentences.text: Age:- According to the petitioner, he was aged 49 years as on the date of accident.
In order to substantiate the same, the petitioner has not produced any document.
The Xerox copy of Aadhaar card available on record shows the year of birth of petitioner as 1972.
The accident was occurred on 22.08.2021.
Hence, it appears to this tribunal that the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 49 years.
Accordingly, the age of the petitioner is considered as 49 years.
18. Income:- According to the petitioner, he was a carpenter by profession and he was earning a sum of Rs.1,000/- per day.
Per-contra, the 3rd respondent has denied the income of petitioner.
To substantiate his income the petitioner has not placed any documentary evidence.

At this juncture, it is worth to rely on the decision of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka decided in M.F.A. No.101144 of 2020 ( MV-I) on 05.07.2023, between Ananda Vs. Arun and Another, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka at Para 9 (b) as hereunder:
"
In the absence of any cogent material on record, it is for the courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant".

19. In the absence of reliable document and supportive evidence, the notional income of the petitioner is to be considered by relying on the judgment of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka referred to above.
As per the notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority for the accident in the year 2021 is Rs.15,000/- per month.
In the instant case the accident occurred on 22.08.2021.
By applying the method adopted by Karnataka State Legal Service Authority, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,000/- per month.
20. Loss of Future Income due to disability:-

According to the petitioner, he has sustained right hip central fractural dislocation,
T2 DM and injuries to other parts of the body.
In order to substantiate the same, he has relied on Ex.P.7 and Ex.P.10.

It is relevant to mention that, respondent No.3 has disputed the injuries caused to P.W.1.
21.
In order to prove the physical disability/injuries, the petitioner examined medical witness namely Dr. Nagaraj B.N., Orthopedic Surgeon at Sai ortho and Dental Senter as P.W.2.
This witness has filed the affidavit in lieu of oral evidence.
In his affidavit he has stated that, the petitioner has came to him for the assessment of disability.

On examination, the petitioner has antalgic gait,
restricted right hip movements, wasting of the right thigh muscles.
Further deposed that, X-ray of right hip shows consolidated floor of the right hip with early OA changes in the right hip joint.
Finally he has assessed the total disability of petitioner at 48% to the right lower limb and 16% to the whole body.
P.W.2 has produced Ex.P.11, the clinical record and Ex.P.12, the X-ray film.
He was cross-examined from the side of 3rd respondent at length.

During the course of cross-examination,
he has deposed that, he has taken opinion from the treated doctor.

He has not examined the Raju Chapparamane vs Universal Sampo Gen Ins Co Ltd on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60763186/
6 inpatient record.

sentences.text: He also admitted that, petitioner has not undergone any surgery.
He also admitted that, the complications referred in the affidavit are not mentioned in the medical records pertaining to the petitioner.
He also admitted that, he has assessed only physical disability and not functional disability.
He has expressed his ignorance regarding the avocation of petitioner.

22. On perusal of the discharge summary of petitioner and evidence of medical witness coupled with wound certificate clearly reveals that, petitioner has sustained right hip central fractural dislocation T2 DM and the said injury is grievous in nature.
As such, the petitioner has suffered grievous injury and physical deformity.
According to the petitioner, he was a carpenter by profession.
He has not produced any documents to substantiate his avocation.
Moreover, PW.2 has assessed the physical disability and not the functional disability.
However, by considering the avocation of petitioner and injuries, the physical disability assessed by the P.W.2 is on higher side.
Moreover, P.W.2 has admitted that, there is no surgery conducted to the petitioner.
Hence, this Tribunal is considered the physical deformity of the petitioner/injured as 6% to the whole body.
23. As discussed supra, age of the injured is considered as 49 years and his income is considered as Rs.15,000/- per month.
Annual income comes to Rs.1,80,000/-(15,000 x 12).
Hence, the proper multiplier applicable to the age of injured as per Sarala Verma case is 13.
If we multiplied yearly income with proper multiplier (1,80,000 X 13), then it comes to Rs.23,40,000/-.
Already this Tribunal has considered the disability of petitioner as 6% to the whole body.
comes to Rs.1,40,400/-.
The said amount of Rs.1,40,400/- is awarded to the Injured/Petitioner under the head of loss of Future Income due to disability.
24. Medical Expenses:-

According to the petitioner, he has incurred Rs.3,50,000/- towards medical,
conveyance and nourishment expenses.

In order to substantiate the incurring of medical expenses,
the petitioner has produced 22 medical bills marked as Ex.P.8 for Rs.1,27,444.71 and 4 medical prescriptions as Ex.P.9.
This Tribunal has carefully perused the medical bills.
Apart from that, there is no evidence from the side of respondents to disbelieve the medical bills.
After careful perusal of the medical bills, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,27,445/-, towards medical expenses.
25. Pain and suffering:-

According to the petitioner, immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Colombia Asia Hospital, Bangalore after first he was shifted to St. Theresa's Hospital, Bangalore wherein he has taken treatment as an inpatient for the right hip central fractural dislocation T2DM.
Already this Tribunal has observed that, the petitioner has undergone skeletal traction.
The petitioner has sustained pain because of said injuries and treatment taken by him.

Apart from that,
as per the evidence of doctor, it appears to this tribunal that, the petitioner has sustained physical deformity.
As per Ex.P.7 the petitioner was admitted to hospital on 22.08.2021 and discharged on 26.08.2021.
Hence, the petitioner has suffered a lot of pain and inconvenience due to accidental injuries.
Therefore, by considering all these aspects, the Tribunal grants compensation of Rs.50,000/- under the head of Pain and Sufferings.

26. Loss of income during the laid up period:-

sentences.text: Already this Tribunal has observed that, the petitioner has sustained right hip central fractural dislocation.
P.W.1 has averred that, he has taken treatment as an inpatient from 22.08.2021 to 26.08.2021 for the period of 5 days and it is evident from Ex.P.7.
P.W.1 has further stated that, again he was admitted to St. Theresa's Hospital on 01.10.2021 for the removal of implants and discharged on 02.10.2021.

Further stated that, as per the advise of the doctors, he took follow-up treatment weekly once for the period of 3 months, 15 days once for the period of 3 months and thereafter once in a month and he has paid Rs.2,000/- per visit.
Naturally it shows that, he might have taken at least two months rest because of the injuries.
He has averred that, he was a carpenter by profession and earning Rs.1,000/- per day.
But he has not produced documents to substantiate the same.
Hence, this Tribunal has already assessed the income of petitioner as Rs.15,000/- per month.
Hence, two months is to be considered as loss of income during laid-up period.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.30,000/- as compensation under the head of loss of income during laid up period.
27. Food, Nourishment and Attendant charges:-
In so for as food, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges are concerned, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatinet for about 5 days i.e., from 22.08.2021 to 26.08.2021.
According to petitioner, as per the advise of the doctors at the time of discharge, he has taken follow-up treatment and physiotherapy treatment continuously.
The petitioner has not produced any documents in this regard.

Hence, looking to the injuries sustained and the period of treatment taken by the petitioner, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.10,000/- under the head of Food, Nourishment and Atttendant charges.
28. Loss of future amenities and happiness:- The petitioner was aged about 49 years at the time of accident.
Already this Tribunal has observed that, the petitioner has sustained right hip central fractural dislocation.
P.W.2 in his affidavit stated that, the petitioner has antalgic gait, restricted right hip movements and wasting of the right thigh muscles.
Therefore, petitioner has to live with the said deformity for the rest of his life.
Therefore, he might have suffered discomforts in life and loss of amenities.
By considering the age, nature of injuries, percentage of disabiltiy, Rs.20,000/- is awarded under this head.
29. Future medical expenses:-
The petitioner has examined the medical witness as P.W.2.
In his affidavit, P.W.2 has stated that, petitioner needs total hip replacement at early stage.

In this regard,
the petitioner or PW.2 have not produced any documents or estimation bill.
Moreover as per the admission of P.W.1, implants have been removed.
Hence, the petitioner is not entitled for compensation towards future medical expenses.

30. Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:

31. Regarding liability and interest.
Driving License:-
According to respondsent No.3, the driver of offending vehicle has no valid driving licence to drive the vehicle.
It is relevant to note that, charge sheet submitted by IO does not reveals that driver of offending vehicle was driving the vehicle without valid and effective DL.
Therefore, it can be inferred that, the driver of the offending vehicle was holding valid D.L. to drive the offending vehicle at the time of accident.
Insurance Policy and liability:-
In the instant case, respondent No.3 has denied the issuance of insurance policy with respect to Car bearing Reg.No.KA-04-MW-9940.
To substantiate the said contentions, the 3rd respondent neither examined any witness nor produced any documents.

Moreover, 1st respondent namely Universal Sompo General Insurance Company filed its written statement, wherein they have specifically conended that, ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company has issued the policy bearing No.3001/MI- 08144220/00/000 and it is valid from 24.10.2019 to 23.10.2022.
In the instant case accident took place on 22.08.2021.

Apart from that,
during the course of cross- examination of P.W.1, there is no denial suggestion with regard to the policy.
Therefore, it appears to this Tibunal that, respondent No.3 has issued the policy to the offending vehicle and same was in force as on the date of accident.
Hence, the respondent No.3 shall pay compenation amount to the petitioner.

32. In view of the decision reported in MFA NO: 30131- 2019 dtd, 12.5.2020 and M.F.A.No.100090/2014 C/w M.F.A.No.25107/2013 between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and Others Vs.
Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and Another, rate of interest on the compensation amount is awarded at 6% p.a. from the date of petition.
